html:
A separatist conflict in the Casamance region of southern Senegal, cut off from the north by the Gambia, which began in 1982 when the Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance (MFDC) called for independence.

The region, mostly Jola, Christian and animist as well as Muslim, felt neglected and dominated by the Wolof north. Fighting, ambushes and landmines killed thousands over the decades and drove many from their villages, some into Guinea-Bissau and the Gambia. Ceasefires came and went; since 2014 the war has been mostly quiet, and in 2022 the army cleared rebel bases. The Le Joola ferry, lost in 2002, was the region's lifeline by sea.
sum: A separatist conflict in the Casamance region of southern Senegal, cut off from the north by the Gambia, which began in 1982 when the Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance (MFDC) called for independence.
